summary: Preinstall dropper fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: @ornikar/babel-preset-base@6.0.13 declares a `preinstall` hook (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases (pinned at v1.3.13), extracts it to a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB single-line, heavily obfuscated bundle (string-array rotation via a `WV8StW` decoder, hex-mangled identifiers, no readable strings) shipped alongside a 787-byte `index.js` that constitutes the actual Babel preset. A Babel preset has no legitimate need to fetch a separate JavaScript runtime at install time to execute an opaque payload; the use of Bun specifically also bypasses Node-based install-time scanners. This matches the alternate-runtime-dropper install-time-RCE pattern: on `npm install`, attacker-controlled code contained in `math_init.js` runs on the installer's machine under a fetched runtime, with the concealment cover of a widely-used package name and scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
